Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary of assessment findings consistent with known heart failure with decompensation: progressive dyspnea over weeks, worse with minimal exertion, ankle edema, dry cough; stable saturations and BP during visit
- Differential diagnoses considered and aligned with transcript:
  - Acute decompensated heart failure (acute fluid overload) — High likelihood; management planned includes increased diuretic therapy and echocardiography to assess pumping function
  - Acute coronary syndrome / myocardial ischemia — Moderate likelihood; prior MI history; to be considered/evaluated if clinically indicated
  - Infection (atypical pneumonia/acute bronchitis) or COPD/exacerbation — Moderate likelihood; dry cough and smoking history; less likely given absence of fever or focal findings
- Note on contradictions: No contradictions between transcript and DDx identified (no “conflict noted”)

Management Plan
- Management plan main: Increase furosemide dosage (from 1 tablet daily to 2 tablets daily for initial days); proceed with blood tests (CBC and kidney function) and echocardiogram; arrange follow-up in about one week; advise on red flags and earlier contact if symptoms worsen (chest pain, palpitations, dizziness)
